headline: Highest risk is data leakage and capability conflict: a local game-playing agent with no egress paired with a shell/network-enabled RAG agent that handles secrets and writes files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A has no shared channel or IO surfaces, so it cannot directly inject B by default. B does have stdin/stdout and file inputs, but the pair lacks a documented bridge from A to B; any prompt-injection path would require unusual manual copy/paste or external wiring. Uncertainty is limited, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A's text into B's prompt or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting A outputs into B prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared folder.
Add a review step before B consumes external text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B reads files, writes files, and has allowlisted network egress while handling configuration secrets. If A and B share a workspace or B ingests A-produced artifacts, B can leak those artifacts or secrets to external services. The pairwise risk exists in common local-dev setups, though not proven by direct shared-state evidence.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem or workspace, B can read A-produced files.
IF B sends retrieved context to allowlisted external APIs, secrets in that context can leave the environment.
mitigations: Store secrets outside any shared workspace.
Separate A and B into different directories.
Restrict B's allowlisted egress to required endpoints only.
Redact secrets before B reads files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is effectively non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces, while B can execute shell commands, install packages, read and write files, and spawn subprocesses. There is no direct evidence of shared locking or shared mutable state, but if both operate on the same directory, B can overwrite artifacts or race with other instances. The uncertainty favors medium because the write surface is real.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF multiple B instances run concurrently without locking, they can race on shared artifacts.
mitigations: Use separate output directories per agent.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Add file locks around shared artifacts.
Make A outputs read-only.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a game-playing repo with no documented output channel, so it is not clearly feeding B. However, B's agentic RAG workflow and API surface suggest it may consume upstream text or retrieved content as authoritative. If A-generated artifacts are fed into B without verification, B could propagate errors into downstream answers or actions. The interaction is inferred, so medium fits.
conditions: IF A outputs are ingested by B as source material, B may treat them as authoritative.
IF B is configured to act on retrieved or upstream text without verification, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require citation checks before B uses external text.
Insert a human review step for B outputs.
Limit B to read-only summarization tasks.
Log source provenance for all inputs.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and touches no data classes, so it is not the compliance driver. B handles academic papers, paper metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets, and its docs mention local development plus elevated privileges and secret handling. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch if sensitive course data or secrets are processed outside intended controls, though no specific jurisdictional breach is documented.
conditions: IF B processes regulated or institutionally sensitive papers under stricter retention rules, its local-dev handling may violate policy.
IF secrets are logged or retained in notebooks or outputs, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B's workspace.
Rotate any exposed secrets immediately.
Disable verbose logging for secret-bearing runs.
Delete notebook outputs after use.
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls.
